{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In the current public SCOPe release 2.08, the canonical nucleosome proteins H2A, H2B, H3, and H4—and variants such as the macro-H2A.1 histone domain—belong to the same Nucleosome core histones family, a.22.1.1 (sunid 47114). This family-level grouping is the strongest SCOPe evidence here for close evolutionary relationship.

More distant histone-fold relatives occupy separate families within the Histone-fold superfamily a.22.1 (sunid 47113): archaeal histones, a.22.1.2 (sunid 47129); TBP-associated factors and related transcription proteins, a.22.1.3 (sunid 47134), including TAF4/TAF12 histone-fold domains, NF-YB/NF-YC, NC2 alpha/beta, and the histone domain of Son of sevenless; and bacterial histone-fold proteins, a.22.1.4 (sunid 101318), including Aq_328. A shared superfamily supports probable distant homology of the classified domains, but it does not make these proteins equivalent nucleosomal histones or justify transferring chromatin, DNA-wrapping, transcriptional, or interaction functions between them.

All four families lie in the Histone-fold fold a.22 (sunid 47112) and the all-alpha class a (sunid 46456). Fold-level similarity alone is weaker evidence and need not establish common ancestry; class-level agreement merely describes broad secondary-structure composition and is not evidence of homology.

Names can be misleading. Linker histones H1/H5 and Hho1p are in family a.4.5.13, within the winged-helix superfamily a.4.5 and DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical-bundle fold a.4, so SCOPe does not place their globular domains in the core histone-fold lineage. H-NS “histone-like” proteins instead form superfamily a.155.1/fold a.155; their relationship to histones is functional analogy rather than SCOPe homology. Histone methyltransferases, acetyltransferases, and deacetylases found by a name search are enzymes acting on histones, not histone relatives by that fact.

For template selection, prefer a same-family structure with matching domain boundaries, length, oligomeric state, and complex context. Archaeal, bacterial, TAF, NF-Y, or NC2 domains can be remote templates for the histone-fold core, but not automatically for nucleosome assembly or function; H1/H5 and H-NS are inappropriate core-histone templates. A representative set should sample each relevant a.22.1 family rather than treating one core histone as representative of the whole superfamily.
